successCriteria.description: Cancelling an APPROVED leave request inserts a NEW leave_requests row (status CANCELLED, reversesRequestId = the original request's id) and issues ZERO update calls against the original row; the original row still reads status APPROVED with its approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt unchanged.

The new reversal row carries employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate and reason copied from the original; status CANCELLED; reversesRequestId = original.id; requestedDays = 0; approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt and decidedAt all null; cancelledBy = actor.id; cancelledAt set.

The balance release happens exactly once per APPROVED cancellation: usedDays is decremented by the ORIGINAL row's requestedDays (not the reversal's 0), pendingDays is untouched, the balance row is read with forUpdate = true before the write, and exactly one balance update call is made.
Cancelling a request whose status is already CANCELLED throws ConflictError (409, code CONFLICT) before any work: no insert, no balance read/write, no audit record, no notification.

The APPROVED reversal path runs inside exactly one uow.withTransaction callback (uow.callCount === 1) with the transaction client forwarded to the reversal insert, the balance read and write, the audit record and the notification create.

Exactly one CANCEL audit record is written for a reversal (AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType 'leave_request', entityId = the ORIGINAL request id, beforeState = the original row, afterState = the new reversal row) and exactly one synchronous cancellation notification is created for the original request's employeeId.

The DRAFT path (no balance read or write) and the SUBMITTED path (pendingDays -= requestedDays, in-place update to CANCELLED) behave exactly as before, and the existing authorization (assertCanCancel), timing (startDate <= today → ConflictError) and NotFoundError guards still hold.
npm run build is clean, the existing Jest suite is green, and npm run smoke is green.

constraints: Only the APPROVED branch of LeaveService.cancel may change. The actor/authorization guards (assertCanCancel), the startDate <= today timing guard, the DRAFT path, the SUBMITTED path, the single uow.withTransaction wrapping, and the client threading through every repository/service call must remain byte-for-byte as they are today.
The APPROVED original row is immutable: no repository.update call may be issued against it, and its status, approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt must not be written by any path in this phase.
The balance release must use the ORIGINAL row's requestedDays and must occur exactly once — no double release, no skipped release, and no release ledger.
A request whose status is already CANCELLED must be rejected with ConflictError (409) before any work is done; chained reversals are not implemented.
ILeaveService.cancel's signature must not change, leave.routes.ts must not change, and no reason/comment field may be added to the cancel wire contract.
No new files and no new route; the change is confined to src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (approximately 1 file).

The service owns the unit of work: cancel must use the injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction and must never import a pool, a client, or a module-level db helper; repositories never open BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.
No tests in this phase — Phase 4 owns them; the existing Jest suite must remain green.
outOfScope: Unit tests for the reversal path (immutability, single release, terminality) — Phase 4 owns them.
The real-Postgres smoke stage proving the reversal end-to-end — Phase 5 owns it.

Any change to leave.model.ts, leave.repository.ts, leave.routes.ts, the migration, or ILeaveService.cancel's signature — Phase 2 delivered the model/repository and the route already calls cancel unchanged.
Chained reversals, a release ledger, a reason/comment field on the cancel wire contract, and any server-side collapsing or filtering of reversal rows in list/read paths.
Amending reconciled.json to match the phase-authoritative audit entityId decision — documentation reconciliation is not part of this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: A row is either an original request (reversesRequestId null) or a reversal of one (reversesRequestId = the original's id). Once a row reaches APPROVED its status, approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt are immutable — a reversal never updates it. A reversal row is terminal: it can never be cancelled or reversed again. At most one reversal exists per original request.

A reversal releases the original reservation exactly once, against the accrual period containing the ORIGINAL request's startDate: usedDays -= original.requestedDays, pendingDays untouched. The reversal row itself (requestedDays 0, status CANCELLED) reserves and releases nothing, so it can never trigger a second release.
A reversal writes exactly one CANCEL entry, in the same transaction as the reversal insert, with beforeState = the untouched APPROVED original and afterState = the new CANCELLED reversal row.
A reversal creates exactly one synchronous cancellation notification to the ORIGINAL request's employeeId, in the same transaction as the reversal insert; no notification is sent to the actor.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Unchanged: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; only the requester's direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request (no self-cancellation of one's own APPROVED request). Enforced by assertCanCancel, never inline in the route.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: NotFoundError (404) for an unknown id; ForbiddenError (403) on an authorization failure; ConflictError (409) when startDate <= today, and ConflictError (409) when the request's status is already CANCELLED (terminality). Returns the new CANCELLED reversal row for the APPROVED path, and the updated row for DRAFT/SUBMITTED.

Must accept all 15 LeaveRequest fields (CreateLeaveRequestInput = Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'>), including reversesRequestId, and must be called with the transaction client so the reversal insert joins the caller's unit of work.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBalanceRepository.findByKey(employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, client?, forUpdate?)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: The release read must pass forUpdate = true together with the transaction client so the row lock is taken before the write; a missing balance row surfaces NotFoundError (404) via resolveBalance.
Both must accept and forward the optional trailing PoolClient so the audit record and the notification join the reversal transaction; neither opens its own transaction.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The reversal insert must supply all 15 fields of CreateLeaveRequestInput, including reversesRequestId, matching the LeaveRequest model field names and nullability exactly.

The reversal insert must go through ILeaveRepository.create with the transaction client; the original row must never be passed to ILeaveRepository.update, and reversesRequestId must not be writable via update (FIELD_COLUMNS/UpdateLeaveRequestDto exclude it).

The APPROVED branch must preserve the existing cancel contract: assertCanCancel, the startDate <= today timing guard, the DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place paths, the single uow.withTransaction, and the client threaded to every call.
The reversal row's status must use LeaveStatus.CANCELLED and the audit action must use AuditAction.CANCEL — the canonical enum members, never bare string literals.

The balance release must resolve the accrual period via the shared periodContaining helper (anchored on the employee's hireDate) and read the balance with forUpdate = true before writing, matching the submit/approve/reject pattern.

The transaction boundary must follow the AGENTS.md decision: the service owns the unit of work via the injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction, participating repository/service methods take the client as an optional last parameter, and no repository opens BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

integrationPoints.why: The reversal row is inserted through create (all 15 fields, client threaded); findByReversesRequestId is the already-reversed lookup the terminality/exactly-once guard relies on.
The single balance release reads with forUpdate = true and writes usedDays -= original.requestedDays inside the reversal transaction.
The CANCEL audit record (GP-002) is written in the same transaction with the client forwarded.
The synchronous cancellation notification to the requester is created in the same transaction with the client forwarded.
The whole reversal operation runs inside one withTransaction callback; the service never imports a pool or client directly.
